watersheds-divide-aquifer.alt: Two panels. Seen from above: watershed A is outlined by a dashed line along its divide, the high ground that separates it from watershed B next door. Rain that falls inside the divide runs downhill as runoff into small tributaries, which join a main river that leaves the watershed at its outlet into a lake. Water falling on the far side of the divide drains to watershed B and flows somewhere else. A cut-away side view: rain falls on hills; runoff flows over the land surface into a stream; some water soaks in by infiltration down to the water table. Below the water table is an aquifer, water held underground in the pores of sand, gravel or rock, above a layer of rock that water does not pass through. The watershed is the land surface that drains to the stream; the aquifer is water stored below the ground.
